name: Plug-in capsule
summary: A factory-made living cell that a crane lifts and bolts to a fixed core, so that the owner can swap the cell and keep the structure.
how: Build a fixed core of concrete or steel that holds the stairs, lifts and services.
Make the cell as one prefabricated unit with its bath, bed and fittings.
Fix the cell to the core with a small number of bolts, such as 4, so that a crane can swap it.
Place the cells at different heights and angles around the core to show growth.
Give each cell one round window and keep the cell skin smooth.

origin.note: Kisho Kurokawa completes the Nakagin Capsule Tower with 140 steel cells on two concrete cores.

adoptions.via: Kisho Kurokawa bolts 140 prefabricated capsules to two concrete cores at the Nakagin Capsule Tower.
